first_output.core_understanding:
- Baseline Concept: A projectile launched with initial speed \\(v_0\\) at elevation angle \\(\theta_0\\) moves under the sole influence of gravity (neglecting air drag). Motion along the horizontal \\(x\\)-axis experiences zero acceleration (\\(a_x = 0\\)), maintaining a constant velocity \\(v_x = v_0 \cos\theta_0\\) and displacement \\(x(t) = x_0 + (v_0 \cos\theta_0)t\\). Motion along the vertical \\(y\\)-axis experiences constant downward gravitational acceleration (\\(a_y = -g\\)), yielding \\(v_y(t) = v_0 \sin\theta_0 - gt\\) and \\(y(t) = y_0 + (v_0 \sin\theta_0)t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2\\).
- Time Perspective:
* Initial Launch Instant (\\(t = 0\\)): Projectile launched from \\((x_0, y_0)\\) with velocity components \\(v_{0x} = v_0 \cos\theta_0\\) and \\(v_{0y} = v_0 \sin\theta_0\\).
* Time-Coupled Progression (\\(0 < t < t_{flight}\\)): Time \\(t\\) acts as the common coupling parameter advancing both horizontal position linearly (\\(x \propto t\\)) and vertical position quadratically (\\(y \propto t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2\\)).
- Custom Perspectives:
* Component Independence Perspective: The horizontal displacement \\(x(t)\\) proceeds completely unaffected by gravitational acceleration, while vertical motion \\(y(t)\\) is identical to a 1D vertical free-fall launch.

- Dynamic Stroboscopic Grid: As projectile moves, vertical and horizontal grid lines highlight that horizontal tick spacing remains perfectly uniform (\\(\Delta x = \text{const}\\)) while vertical tick spacing expands and contracts identical to 1D free fall.

first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation:
- استقلالية مركبات حركة المقذوفات: حركة المقذوفات في بعدين هي أبسط وأجمل تطبيق على استقلالية المركبات! لما تشوط كورة بزاوية \\(\theta_0\\) وسرعة \\(v_0\\)، الحركة بتنقسم لحركتين مستقلين تماماً:

first_output.laws_if_any:

first_output.core_understanding:
- Baseline Concept: Vector superposition combines component velocities into the instantaneous velocity vector \\(\mathbf{v}(t) = (v_0 \cos\theta_0)\mathbf{i} + (v_0 \sin\theta_0 - gt)\mathbf{j}\\). The magnitude of velocity (speed) is \\(v(t) = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y(t)^2}\\), and its direction angle relative to the horizontal is \\(\theta(t) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v_y(t)}{v_x}\right)\\). At the trajectory apex, \\(v_y = 0\\), so speed reaches its non-zero minimum value \\(v_{min} = v_x = v_0 \cos\theta_0\\). Throughout the entire flight, the acceleration vector remains strictly constant: \\(\mathbf{a} = 0\mathbf{i} - g\mathbf{j} = -g\mathbf{j}\\).
- Time Perspective:
* Launch (\\(t=0\\)): Speed is maximum \\(v_0\\), angle is launch angle \\(\theta_0\\).
* Apex (\\(t = t_{apex} = \frac{v_0 \sin\theta_0}{g}\\)): Vertical speed drops to zero (\\(v_y = 0\\)), velocity vector becomes purely horizontal \\(\mathbf{v} = v_x \mathbf{i}\\).
* Landing (\\(t = t_{flight}\\)): Vertical speed is restored in downward direction (\\(v_y = -v_0 \sin\theta_0\\)), overall speed returns to initial launch speed \\(v_0\\).
- Custom Perspectives:
* Acceleration Invariance Perspective: While the velocity vector continuously changes magnitude and rotates direction along the curve, the acceleration vector \\(\mathbf{a} = -g\mathbf{j}\\) remains unchanged in magnitude (\\(9.81\text{ m/s}^2\\)) and direction (straight down) at every point, including at the apex.

perspective_map.baseline_objects_and_state: 2D parabolic trajectory canvas, projectile sphere \\(P\\), green velocity vector arrow \\(\mathbf{v}\\), velocity components \\(v_x\mathbf{i}\\) and \\(v_y\mathbf{j}\\), red downward acceleration arrow \\(\mathbf{a} = -9.81\mathbf{j}\text{ m/s}^2\\), speed vs time plot canvas \\(v(t)\\).
perspective_map.time_perspective: Applicable. Progression type: Time parameter sweep \\(t \in [0, 3.26\text{ s}]\\).
perspective_map.custom_perspectives: Acceleration Invariance (\\(\mathbf{a} = -g\mathbf{j}\\) constant in magnitude and direction at all points).
perspective_map.learner_investigations: Learner drags time slider \\(t\\) to trajectory apex \\(t_{apex}\\), witnessing vertical velocity \\(v_y\\) shrink to zero, speed reach minimum \\(v = v_x\\), and acceleration arrow remain constantly downward.
perspective_map.controls: Time cursor slider \\(t\\), Toggle Velocity Vector Component Triangle, Toggle Speed \\(v(t)\\) Plot Canvas.
perspective_map.linked_views: Projectile position on 2D parabolic path directly updates velocity vector orientation, component triangle, and speed curve \\(v(t)\\).
perspective_map.visual_learning_goal: Prove that projectile velocity is the vector sum \\(v_x\mathbf{i} + v_y\mathbf{j}\\), speed is non-zero minimum at apex, and acceleration vector is constantly \\(-g\mathbf{j}\\).
perspective_map.coverage: Fully covers 2D Velocity Vector Superposition, Apex Speed Minimum, Vector Angle Rotation, and Constant Acceleration Invariance.
perspective_map.acceptance_checks: At trajectory apex, velocity readout displays \\(v_y = 0\text{ m/s}\\) and \\(v = v_x\\), while acceleration arrow reads \\(-9.81\mathbf{j}\text{ m/s}^2\\).
perspective_map.evidence_gaps: Magnus effect and spin dynamics excluded.
